Exercise SIEM, CSPM, cloud-native detection, and SOC workflows with real cloud API activity.
Confirm detection rules fire on real technique execution before incident response exercises.

safety_notes: Stratus Red Team is designed for authorized sandbox cloud environments only.

scripts.name: STRATUS - AZURE - Azure Blob Storage ransomware through Encryption Scope using client-managed Key Vault key
scripts.description:
Stratus Red Team cloud adversary-emulation technique for Azure.

Azure Blob Storage ransomware through Encryption Scope using client-managed Key Vault key

Simulates Azure Blob Storage ransomware activity that encrypts files using an encryption scope backed by a customer-managed Key Vault key, then deletes the key to render the data inaccessible. Note that due to Azure's purge protection feature, it is impossible to hard-delete the key and the blobs remain recoverable. You will need to have the Key Vault Administrator role on your Azure subscription to correctly warmup the technique. Warm-up: - Create an Azure Storage Account with a system-assigned

Morgana executes the official Stratus technique using an isolated MORGANA_TEST_ID correlation ID. Prerequisite infrastructure is handled by Stratus warmup. Cleanup uses the same correlation ID.
scripts.command:
# Stratus Red Team — Azure Blob Storage ransomware through Encryption Scope using client-managed Key Vault key
# Correlation ID = Morgana Test ID for Detection Fabric correlation
STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID="${MORGANA_TEST_ID:-$(uuidgen 2>/dev/null || cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid 2>/dev/null || echo manual)}"
export STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID

if [ -n "#{stratus_azure_subscription}" ]; then export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID="#{stratus_azure_subscription}"; fi

# Select Stratus binary for this Agent OS
if command -v stratus >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STRATUS_BIN=stratus
else
  STRATUS_BIN="{{asset:stratus_linux_amd64}}"
  chmod +x "$STRATUS_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "[INFO] Stratus Red Team: technique=azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope"
echo "[INFO] Correlation ID: $STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID"

# Warmup + Detonate
"$STRATUS_BIN" detonate azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope
EXIT_CODE=$?

echo "[INFO] Detonation complete: exit=$EXIT_CODE technique=azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope"
# Emit structured result
echo "MORGANA_RESULT_METADATA={\"provider\":\"stratus-red-team\",\"technique_id\":\"azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope\",\"correlation_id\":\"$STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID\",\"exit_code\":$EXIT_CODE}"
exit $EXIT_CODE
scripts.cleanup_command:
# Stratus Red Team cleanup — uses SAME correlation ID as detonation
# MORGANA_TEST_ID must match the value used during detonate
STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID="${MORGANA_TEST_ID:-manual}"
export STRATUS_RED_TEAM_CORRELATION_ID

if command -v stratus >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STRATUS_BIN=stratus
else
  STRATUS_BIN="{{asset:stratus_linux_amd64}}"
fi

"$STRATUS_BIN" cleanup azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope
CLEANUP_EXIT=$?
echo "[INFO] Cleanup complete: exit=$CLEANUP_EXIT technique=azure.impact.blob-ransomware-client-encryption-scope"
exit $CLEANUP_EXIT

In Azure Storage diagnostic logs, look for: 1. Unusual volume of read (GetBlob) followed by write (PutBlob) operations on the same blobs. 2. PutBlob operations with the x-ms-encryption-algorithm request header set to AES256, indicating customer-provided key usage.
